extracted.intended_audience: QHP issuers (rate filers), State Exchanges, State regulators, and stakeholders responding to the proposed rule
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed regulatory requirements and data-reporting standards for Qualified Health Plan (QHP) issuers' rate filings (URRTs and actuarial memoranda) regarding CSR loading and for State Exchanges electing an SBE-Enhanced Direct Enrollment (SBE-EDE) model, including oversight, privacy, and operational readiness requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report CSR amounts and additional revenue in URRT using recent annual data
rubrics_metrics.description: Issuers that make a plan-level adjustment to account for unreimbursed CSRs must submit CSR amounts paid on behalf of enrollees and the additional revenue collected from the previously applied CSR load in the URRT for the upcoming plan year using the most recent annual data available prior to the applicable filing year, using the standard methodology set forth in §156.430(c)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In most cases the most recent annual CSR data would reflect the plan year two years before the upcoming plan year (example: CSRs paid in PY2025 are reported during 2026 filing year on rate filings for PY2027). The submission should be at the plan level and use the standard methodology for consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use CMS standard methodology to calculate CSR amounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the CMS standard methodology, issuers re-adjudicate the actual complete set of claims incurred by an enrollee in the CSR plan variation as if they had been enrolled in the associated standard plan to determine the difference the enrollee would have paid; the difference equals the amount of CSRs provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS believes the standard methodology is the most accurate method for calculating the actual value of CSRs and that many issuers are familiar with it. The proposal expects issuers to apply this methodology when reporting CSR amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow aggregate plan-level URRT submission (not CSR reconciliation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed URRT data submission would require issuers to submit an aggregate amount of CSRs provided at the plan level on the URRT and would not require issuers to use the CSR reconciliation process implemented by CMS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach is intended to reduce issuer burden compared to policy-level CSR reconciliation submissions that require conforming to business rules, data element validations, and file formats which previously caused multiple submission attempts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include CSR load factor in URRT for each plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Issuers would include in the URRT the applicable CSR load factor for each plan that would be applied to the market adjusted index rate to calculate the calibrated plan adjusted index rate for the upcoming plan year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collection of the CSR load factor is to fulfill responsibility under §156.80(d) that all permitted plan-level adjustments be 'actuarially justified.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Actuarial memorandum must explain methodology for CSR load factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Issuers must include in the actuarial memorandum an explanation of the methodology used to determine the CSR load factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The memorandum should also include an explanation comparing amounts: the additional revenue expected from the applied CSR load, and the expected amount of CSRs that will be paid for enrollees for the upcoming plan year, to allow regulators to determine if the load is actuarially justified and not excessive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report additional revenue expected from CSR load and expected CSRs paid
rubrics_metrics.description: Issuers would include in the URRT the additional revenue expected to be collected from the applied CSR load factor and the expected amount of CSRs that will be paid for enrollees for the upcoming plan year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where provided, issuers should explain in the actuarial memorandum how the expected additional revenue compares to expected CSRs paid; HHS intends to issue guidance in revised Unified Rate Review Instructions on how to submit these fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actuarial justification standard for CSR load factors
rubrics_metrics.description: An actuarially justified CSR load factor is one that is 'calibrated on actual experience' and that only accounts for the projected revenue loss of unreimbursed CSR payments 'without materially exceeding that amount.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS will use submitted data (paid CSRs, revenue from prior CSR loads, expected CSRs and expected load revenue, methodology) to determine whether CSR loads are actuarially justified as plan-level adjustments under §156.80.

rubrics_metrics.name: URRT must include historical and projected claims experience
rubrics_metrics.description: The collection of CSR-related data is captured under §154.215(d)(1), which states that historical and projected claims experience must be included in the URRT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS is not proposing regulatory text changes because these data collections are already captured by existing URRT requirements; comments requested on proposal to require CSR load reporting beginning with PY2027.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan-level CSR adjustments permissible only if actuarially justified and state-permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Per §156.80(d)(2)(i), plan-level adjustments to account for unreimbursed CSR payments are permissible only if actuarially justified and permitted by the applicable State authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS will provide regulators the data necessary to assess compliance with §156.80 and to ensure CSR loads are not inflating Federal expenditures (PTC) or undermining Federal rating rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discontinue standardized plan options (regulatory removal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to discontinue the full suite of standardized plan option policies effective beginning in PY2027, including removal of definitions and regulatory requirements pertaining to standardized options and their differential display on HealthCare.gov and partner sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a regulatory change proposal (removal/redesignation of certain regulatory paragraphs); HHS will cease annual design and publication of standardized plan options in Payment Notices if finalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove prior-SBE-FP operation requirement for States seeking to operate a State Exchange
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to remove §155.105(b)(4), rescinding the requirement that a State seeking to operate a State Exchange must first operate for at least 1 plan year as a State-based Exchange on the Federal platform (SBE-FP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS recognizes some States have infrastructure enabling direct implementation and that requiring prior SBE-FP operation could create unnecessary barriers; seeks comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescind requirement to provide supporting documentation upon request for Blueprint progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose amending §155.106(a)(2) to rescind the codified requirement that States must provide, upon request, supporting documentation demonstrating progress toward meeting or implementing State Exchange Blueprint requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS notes it has historically requested supplemental documents and will continue to do so as needed, but is proposing to remove the codified 'upon request' requirement to support deregulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow State Exchanges to rely on web-brokers for consumer-facing eligibility/enrollment interfaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose revising §155.205(b) to remove the requirement that all State Exchanges operate a consumer-facing centralized eligibility and enrollment platform on the State Exchange's website so a State Exchange could rely entirely on web-brokers to operate consumer-facing websites facilitating eligibility and enrollment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such web-broker sites must interface with the State Exchange's back-end eligibility and enrollment system using State Exchange-approved technical specifications/standards to transmit applicant information and QHP selection/enrollment seamlessly; the State Exchange would still operate the back-end platform and maintain website responsibilities under §155.205(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards/process for selecting web-brokers and non-Exchange entity requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: State Exchanges that opt to use web-brokers must establish standards and a process for selecting web-brokers similar to the standards/criteria for direct enrollment entities (§§155.221(j) and 155.220(n)), including requiring a non-Exchange web-broker entity to satisfy all requirements under §155.110(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures selected web-brokers meet minimum entity qualifications and that interfaces and responsibilities mirror direct enrollment safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Exchanges retain responsibility for eligibility determinations and enrollment records
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if consumer-facing webpages are operated by web-brokers, State Exchanges remain responsible for making all eligibility determinations for QHP coverage and related insurance affordability programs and for maintaining records of all QHP enrollments on the Exchange.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State Exchanges must obtain HHS approval for the eligibility application used on consumer websites per §155.405 and demonstrate appropriate functionality for accurate determinations; enrollment via web-brokers is considered enrollment through the Exchange per §155.220(c)(3) and proposed §155.221(k)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: SBE-EDE web-brokers must meet privacy, security, accessibility, and LEP protections
rubrics_metrics.description: All consumer data collected, stored, or transmitted through web-broker platforms operating under SBE-EDE remain subject to privacy and security standards at §155.260; web-brokers would be subject to HHS oversight and monitoring pursuant to §155.280; State Exchanges must ensure web-brokers comply with protections including encryption, access controls, and audit logging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Web-brokers and State Exchanges must also meet Federal accessibility standards under §155.205(c) for individuals with disabilities and requirements for individuals with limited English proficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use SMART and external audits for SBE-EDE oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: State Exchanges implementing SBE-EDE would be required to complete SMART submissions annually attesting compliance with Exchange operational requirements under §155.1200(b) and to engage independent qualified auditing entities to perform annual external financial and programmatic audits under §155.1200(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS will review SMART submissions, issue formal letters on noncompliance, and identify corrective actions; additional oversight tools include technical assistance and ongoing communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Exchange website must list standardized comparative QHP information and quality ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: In connection with SBE-EDE, the State Exchange must make available a website listing basic QHP information for comparison and a listing with links to approved partner websites; comparative plan information must use a standardized format including the uniform summary of benefits and coverage and must include quality ratings assigned to each QHP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This meets statutory minimums for consumer information and supports consumer shopping even if enrollment occurs on partner sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBE-EDE operational readiness, timing, and approval process
rubrics_metrics.description: A State Exchange electing SBE-EDE must submit an Exchange Blueprint application or revision to HHS for review at least 15 months prior to the targeted open enrollment launch date as SBE-EDE; HHS would have up to 90 days to review and approve or deny the revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The State Exchange must demonstrate operational readiness to enroll qualified individuals in a manner that constitutes enrollment through the Exchange and enable APTC and CSR applications and Medicaid/CHIP assessments/determinations using the HHS-approved eligibility application per §155.405; revisions are evaluated under §155.105(e) and §155.105(c)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: State Exchanges must continue certain Exchange functions despite SBE-EDE
rubrics_metrics.description: A State Exchange electing SBE-EDE would continue to be responsible for functions such as providing an electronic calculator, establishing a Navigator program, providing a toll-free hotline, performing Medicaid/CHIP assessments or determinations, and ensuring accurate APTC payments and reconciliation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State Exchanges must share eligibility determination and enrollment information in coordination with issuers and HHS (see §§155.340, 155.400, 155.430) to support payments and reconciliations.

rubrics_metrics.name: EDE partners must meet all applicable statutory and regulatory requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: EDE partners (web-brokers) must meet all applicable statutory and regulatory requirements governing application for and enrollment in QHPs; the State Exchange must ensure approved partners meet requirements and are overseen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS oversight authority under §155.1200 remains; approved partners will be listed with links on Exchange websites; States may initially pilot SBE-EDE to gather operational experience prior to broader application.
